create.title: Create
create.intro: The universal generation workspace. Generate images, videos, and audio using cloud APIs or fully-local open-source models.

steps.title: 1 · Choose Source
steps.body: Select Cloud APIs (FAL.ai, Replicate, etc.) for fastest results, or Local open-source for free unlimited generation on your own machine.

steps.title: 2 · Pick a Kind
steps.body: Choose Image, Video, or Audio. The model list updates automatically to show only models that support your chosen output type.

steps.title: 3 · Select a Model
steps.body: Each model has different strengths. Flux Pro is great for photorealism. Kling/Seedance for video. WAN for animation. Open the Models tab to compare.

steps.title: 4 · Write Your Prompt
steps.body: Be specific and visual — describe the subject, lighting, mood, camera angle, and key details. Example: 'Cinematic close-up of a woman in a rain-soaked Tokyo alley, neon reflections, shallow depth of field, 8K.'

steps.title: 5 · Apply Controls
steps.body: Camera Move adds cinematic motion. Visual Style applies a preset aesthetic. Character Lock and Location Lock maintain consistent identities and environments across generations.

steps.title: 6 · Add Reference Images
steps.body: Upload Style, Subject, Color, or Composition references to guide the model visually. Upload to the matching slot for best results. Only ref-capable models use them.

tips: Add 'cinematic, 8K, ultra detailed, sharp focus' at the end of your prompt to boost quality.
Negative prompt: 'blurry, watermark, low quality, distorted' removes common artifacts.
Combine a Style chip with a strong prompt for consistent, recognizable aesthetics.
Use Character Lock + Location Lock together for story-consistent scene sequences.
apiKeys: FAL.ai — Flux, Kling, Seedance, WAN and more

film.title: Film Studio
film.intro: Direct professional-grade film sequences with full cinematography controls — camera bodies, lenses, film stocks, directors' styles, color palettes, and shot-by-shot continuity.

steps.title: 1 · Create a Project
steps.body: Name your film project and click Create. Or use a Quick-start template — Noir Crime Thriller, Sci-Fi Epic, Fashion Editorial, Horror, Music Video, Documentary — to get going instantly with pre-configured shots.

steps.title: 2 · Set the Project Look
steps.body: Film Style, Director's Style, Color Palette, and Grain apply to every shot in the project. Set these first to lock the overall visual language.

steps.title: 3 · Add Shots
steps.body: Each shot card has its own prompt, camera move, camera body, lens, character, and location lock. This lets you build a complete cinematic sequence shot by shot.

steps.title: 4 · Lock Characters & Locations
steps.body: Create reusable identities in the Characters tab and environments in the Locations tab. Assign them to individual shots for perfect consistency across the sequence.

steps.title: 5 · Generate Shot by Shot
steps.body: Hit Generate Shot on each card. Images and videos are automatically saved to your Library.

steps.title: 6 · Export to DaVinci Resolve
steps.body: Use Send to Resolve to push generated clips directly into your editing timeline via the Resolve bridge.

tips: Set Film Style + Color Palette at the project level, then vary camera moves per shot for dynamic sequences.
Director's Style adds the strongest visual fingerprint — 'Denis Villeneuve' vs 'Wes Anderson' are night and day.
Use Shot Mood Color to create emotional arcs across scenes using color psychology.
Mix image and video shots in the same project for a combined still + motion storyboard.

fashion.title: Fashion Studio
fashion.intro: Create editorial fashion visuals, outfit concepts, try-on imagery, and lookbooks with full AI-powered fashion production tools.

steps.title: 1 · Pick a Tool
steps.body: Choose from Fashion Editorial, Virtual Try-On, Style Transfer, Lookbook Generator, or other specialized fashion tools in the grid.

steps.title: 2 · Set Fashion Style
steps.body: Select your aesthetic — Avant-Garde, Streetwear, Haute Couture, Minimalist, Y2K, and more — from the Fashion Style dropdown.

steps.title: 3 · Choose Pose & Lighting
steps.body: Combine a pose style (power stance, editorial recline, candid motion) with a lighting mood (golden hour, studio, dramatic chiaroscuro).

steps.title: 4 · Upload References
steps.body: Use the Reference Images panel to upload Clothing, Shoes, Hair, and Overall Look references. The AI closely matches your uploaded images.

steps.title: 5 · Write Your Brief
steps.body: Describe specific garments, model type, setting, and mood in the Details field. E.g. 'Oversized camel trench coat, model walking on Paris street, autumn, cinematic.'

tips: Clothing reference images give the strongest results — upload the exact garment whenever possible.
'Editorial lighting' + 'Haute Couture' style = high-end magazine look consistently.
Hair references significantly improve model head-shot consistency.
Use Character Lock to maintain the same face across multiple outfit shots in a lookbook.
apiKeys: FAL.ai — best image quality for fashion

product.title: Product Studio
product.intro: Create professional product photos, lifestyle imagery, and e-commerce visuals without a physical studio or photographer.

steps.title: 1 · Upload Your Product
steps.body: Use the Product Photo reference slot to upload your actual product image. A clean white-background photo gives the best results.

steps.title: 2 · Choose a Tool
steps.body: Ghost Mannequin for apparel, Background Replace for e-commerce shots, Lifestyle Scene to place the product in a real environment, or 360° Turntable for multiple angles.

steps.title: 3 · Add Context References
steps.body: Upload Lifestyle Context images (e.g. a kitchen for a food product) and Background references for the desired scene.

steps.title: 4 · Describe the Scene
steps.body: Describe lighting, surface, props, and mood. E.g. 'Marble surface, dramatic side lighting, minimalist white background, luxury feel.'

steps.title: 5 · Generate & Iterate
steps.body: Generate multiple options and fine-tune with more specific references or adjusted prompts.

tips: Product on clean white background input gives the cleanest output.
For lifestyle shots, specify season and time of day: 'summer morning, kitchen counter, bright natural light.'
'Flat lay, overhead shot, product centered' = e-commerce-ready images instantly.
Multiple generations from the same references are great for A/B testing ad creatives.

marketing.title: Marketing Studio
marketing.intro: Generate scroll-stopping ad creatives, social media visuals, banners, and campaign assets at scale — no designer needed.

steps.title: 1 · Define Your Goal
steps.body: Are you making a social ad, banner, email hero image, or print piece? Select the appropriate tool for your format.

steps.title: 2 · Upload Brand Assets
steps.body: Add your brand colors, logo, and existing visual assets in the Brand Visual reference slot. This is the most important step for on-brand output.

steps.title: 3 · Add Inspiration
steps.body: Upload competitor ads or reference campaigns you want to study or draw from in the Inspiration slot.

steps.title: 4 · Write the Creative Brief
steps.body: Include the headline concept, call to action, target audience, and key message in the Details field.

steps.title: 5 · Generate & Iterate
steps.body: Generate multiple variations and pick the strongest. Adjust prompt and references for each round of iteration.

tips: Describe your target audience explicitly in the prompt — it changes the energy of the image.
Brand reference + Mood Board together produce the most on-brand results.
Specify the platform ratio: '9:16 for TikTok', '4:5 for Instagram Feed', '1:1 for Meta ads.'
Include 'bold text overlay space at bottom' in the prompt for ad-ready images with CTA room.

shorts.title: Shorts Studio
shorts.intro: Create viral short-form video content for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other vertical platforms.

steps.title: 1 · Define Your Hook
steps.body: The first 3 seconds are everything. Describe a visually arresting opening frame in the Hook reference slot and in your prompt.

steps.title: 2 · Write or Generate Script
steps.body: Use the AI Script tool to generate a complete short-form script with hook, body, and CTA in under 60 seconds of spoken content.

steps.title: 3 · Generate Clips
steps.body: Create individual clips for each section of the script. Shorter 3-5 second clips with sharp cuts work best for the algorithm.

steps.title: 4 · Always Use 9:16
steps.body: Set aspect ratio to 9:16 for all vertical platforms. Never use 16:9 for short-form — it will be cropped badly on mobile.

steps.title: 5 · Maintain Visual Style
steps.body: Upload a style reference to ensure consistent color and aesthetic across your entire content library.

tips: 9:16 aspect ratio is mandatory — every TikTok, Reel, and Short is vertical.
The first frame must create instant curiosity or surprise — describe it with extreme specificity.
Consistent color grading (via Color Reference) makes your content recognizable as a creator brand.
Upload your best-performing video as a style reference to replicate what already works.

explainer.title: Explainer Studio
explainer.intro: Build explainer videos, educational content, tutorials, and animated presentations that communicate complex ideas clearly.

steps.title: 1 · Define the Topic
steps.body: Be specific about what you're explaining and to whom. 'How blockchain works for non-technical CFOs' is much better than 'blockchain.'

steps.title: 2 · Generate a Script
steps.body: Use the AI Script Generator for a structured script: intro hook, 3 key points, clear conclusion, and CTA.

steps.title: 3 · Set the Visual Style
steps.body: Upload art/animation style references — flat design, whiteboard, motion graphics, 3D animation, or photorealistic.

steps.title: 4 · Create Section Visuals
steps.body: Generate a supporting visual for each section of the explainer. Keep each visual focused on ONE key idea.

steps.title: 5 · Add a Character
steps.body: Use Character Lock if you have a presenter or mascot who appears throughout all sections.

tips: Keep each visual to ONE key concept — never try to explain two things in one image.
Whiteboard animation style is universally understood and never goes out of style.
Match the visual complexity to your audience — casual for consumers, clean corporate for enterprise.
Slide-style references produce more structured, education-forward output.

influencer.title: Influencer Studio
influencer.intro: Create influencer-style content, personal branding visuals, sponsored post imagery, and lifestyle photography at scale.

steps.title: 1 · Define the Persona
steps.body: Describe the influencer persona — niche (fitness, fashion, travel, tech), aesthetic, audience age, and platform.

steps.title: 2 · Upload Outfit & Pose References
steps.body: Outfit and pose references are the most impactful uploads for influencer content. Be specific with each.

steps.title: 3 · Lock Identity
steps.body: Create a Character in the Characters tab to lock the face and identity consistently across all posts. This is essential for creator brands.

steps.title: 4 · Lock Location
steps.body: Use Location Lock to maintain a consistent environment for your feed aesthetic — e.g. always the same Paris apartment look.

steps.title: 5 · Generate at Scale
steps.body: Create batches of content for different formats (grid post, story, reel thumbnail) from the same session.

tips: Outfit references are critical — upload the exact clothing item for best matching.
Consistent lighting style (golden hour, clean studio) builds an instantly recognizable brand.
Mix close-up portraits and wide environmental shots for natural feed variety.
1:1 for Instagram grid, 9:16 for Stories and Reels — always generate both formats.

voice.title: Voice Studio
voice.intro: Generate professional voiceovers, AI narration, sound effects, ambient audio, and music for your creative projects.

steps.title: 1 · Write Your Script
steps.body: Prepare the exact text to narrate. Clear, well-punctuated scripts give the best audio. Include stage directions in brackets: [pause] [excited].

steps.title: 2 · Specify Voice Style
steps.body: Describe the voice in detail: 'Warm, authoritative, slightly British, documentary narrator.' The more specific, the more accurate.

steps.title: 3 · Choose a Model
steps.body: Different providers offer different voice qualities. Try 2-3 options and compare. Some excel at character voices, others at clean narration.

steps.title: 4 · Generate & Preview
steps.body: Generate and review the audio. Re-run with adjusted instructions for different tone, pace, or emphasis.

steps.title: 5 · Export to Film Studio
steps.body: Audio files save to your Library for use in Film Studio projects or external editors.

tips: Commas and ellipses create natural breathing pauses — use them liberally.
Short bursts under 60 seconds give the cleanest, most consistent results.
Use Character voice associations to maintain the same voice across all project audio.
Add [enthusiastic] or [whispering] in brackets to inject emotion at specific moments.

apps.title: Apps Studio
apps.intro: Generate app UI mockups, icon sets, splash screens, app store screenshots, and promotional assets for mobile and web apps.

steps.title: 1 · Choose Asset Type
steps.body: App Icon, UI Screenshot, App Store Banner, Splash Screen, or UI Flow Diagram — each tool has a specialized output format.

steps.title: 2 · Upload UI References
steps.body: Upload existing screenshots or Dribbble/Behance design references to guide the visual direction accurately.

steps.title: 3 · Upload Brand Colors
steps.body: Upload your logo and brand color palette in the Brand reference slot for on-brand output.

steps.title: 4 · Describe the App
steps.body: Name the app, describe its core purpose, and specify the exact screen or element. E.g. 'Social fitness app — home feed screen with workout cards, dark mode, iOS.'

steps.title: 5 · Generate & Refine
steps.body: Generate multiple options and select the strongest. Adjust platform, mode (dark/light), and style specifics to refine.

tips: Always specify 'iOS style' or 'Material Design' or 'custom' for consistent UI language.
App icon reference uploads give dramatically better results than prompts alone.
Dark mode and light mode need separate explicit generations — never assume.
For screenshots, describe UI elements to show: 'navigation bar, card grid, floating action button.'

appbuild.title: App Building
appbuild.intro: Generate functional code for web and mobile apps, build components, write backend logic, and create full-stack applications with Claude AI.

steps.title: 1 · Describe What to Build
steps.body: Be highly specific: 'A React authentication form with email/password, validation, error states, loading spinner, and a success redirect.' Not just 'a login form.'

steps.title: 2 · Upload UI References
steps.body: Screenshot the design you want to replicate — Claude will code to match it precisely. This is the fastest path to accurate UI code.

steps.title: 3 · Specify Your Tech Stack
steps.body: Always mention the stack: 'React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Next.js App Router.' Never assume Claude knows your project's framework.

steps.title: 4 · Review Generated Code
steps.body: Output appears in the result panel. Review, copy to your IDE, and test. The code is production-ready but always review before shipping.

steps.title: 5 · Iterate With Follow-ups
steps.body: Ask for specific fixes, additions, or refactoring in the Details field for subsequent generations.

tips: More context = better code. Include existing component names and patterns when asking for additions.
Ask explicitly for TypeScript types if your project uses TypeScript — it won't assume.
'Production-ready with error handling and loading states' in the prompt produces much more robust output.
For full pages, break into smaller components and generate each one separately for best results.
apiKeys: Anthropic — Claude powers all code generation

designdocs.title: Design Docs
designdocs.intro: Create wireframes, design system documentation, product specs, PRDs, technical specs, and user flow documents.

steps.title: 1 · Choose Document Type
steps.body: PRD, Technical Spec, Wireframe Description, Component API Spec, User Story, or Flow Diagram — each tool has a targeted template.

steps.title: 2 · Give Full Context
steps.body: Describe the product, target user, problem being solved, and any technical constraints. The more context, the more accurate and useful the document.

steps.title: 3 · Upload References
steps.body: Upload design mockups, competitive screenshots, or existing docs to ground the generated content in real examples.

steps.title: 4 · Generate & Review
steps.body: The AI produces a fully structured document with sections, tables, acceptance criteria, and edge cases.

steps.title: 5 · Export
steps.body: Copy the markdown output into Notion, Confluence, Linear, GitHub, or your preferred docs tool.

tips: More product context = dramatically more useful specs. Spend time on the setup.
'Include edge cases, error states, and empty states' adds significant practical value.
Wireframe descriptions work best when you describe each screen's purpose AND key interactions.
Name specific competitor products in your prompt to ground requirements in known UX patterns.

digiproduct.title: Digital Products
digiproduct.intro: Create cover art, landing page heroes, promotional visuals, and mockup images for ebooks, online courses, templates, and SaaS tools.

steps.title: 1 · Upload Your Product
steps.body: Upload a screenshot or draft cover for your digital product in the Product Visual reference slot. This grounds the AI in what you're actually selling.

steps.title: 2 · Choose Output Type
steps.body: Cover Art, Device Mockup, Landing Page Hero, Social Card, or Bundle Visual — each is optimized for its format.

steps.title: 3 · Upload Brand Reference
steps.body: Upload your brand color palette and logo for on-brand output that feels like your existing product family.

steps.title: 4 · Write the Brief
steps.body: Describe the product's purpose and ideal buyer persona — this shapes the emotional message of the visual.

steps.title: 5 · Generate Multiple Options
steps.body: Always generate at least 3 variations to compare. Run A/B tests with your audience to see which converts best.

tips: Mockup context (device frames, desk setups, hands holding screens) makes products feel real and premium.
Dark glowing designs convert well for tech/AI digital products.
Show the product in use — a course cover with a student at a laptop, an ebook on a Kindle.
Generate 1:1 for social and 16:9 for banners from the same session.

spatial.title: 3D & Spatial
spatial.intro: Generate 3D scenes, architectural visualizations, product renders, and spatial art using AI-powered 3D generation tools.

steps.title: 1 · Describe the 3D Scene
steps.body: Be specific about materials, lighting, camera angle, and environment. E.g. '3D render of a minimalist concrete house at dusk, Octane render, soft volumetric shadows, distant mountains.'

steps.title: 2 · Specify Render Engine & Lighting
steps.body: Name a render engine (Octane, Cycles, V-Ray, Unreal Engine) and a lighting setup (HDRI, three-point, golden hour, neon accent). These two things define the entire mood.

steps.title: 3 · Upload Reference
steps.body: For architectural or product work, upload reference photos of buildings, materials, or products you want to match.

steps.title: 4 · Choose the Right Model
steps.body: Some models specialize in photorealistic architecture, others in stylized or abstract 3D. Test 2-3 to find the best fit for your style.

steps.title: 5 · Iterate One Element at a Time
steps.body: 3D prompt crafting is iterative. Change one variable per generation — lighting, then materials, then composition — for controlled results.

tips: Naming a specific render engine transforms results: 'Octane render' alone adds hours of quality.
For architecture, name materials explicitly: 'brushed steel, smoked glass, polished concrete, teak wood.'
'HDRI lighting, golden hour, volumetric god rays' = instant cinematic photorealism.
'Neutral grey gradient background, turntable studio lighting' = perfect product render every time.

touchdesigner.title: TouchDesigner
touchdesigner.intro: Connect God's Pandora to TouchDesigner for real-time generative visuals, audio-reactive art, particle systems, GLSL shaders, and live VJ/installation output via OSC and WebSocket.

steps.title: 1 · Start TouchDesigner
steps.body: Open TouchDesigner on your machine before connecting. TD must be running — God's Pandora sends to it, not the other way around.

steps.title: 2 · Run the Setup Script
steps.body: In TouchDesigner's Textport (F9), paste and run the SETUP_BRIDGE.py script from the public/td-scripts folder. It auto-creates the OSC In CHOP (port 7000) and Web Server DAT (port 9980).

steps.title: 3 · Connect in God's Pandora
steps.body: Open the Config panel in the TouchDesigner tab, enter your TD machine's IP (127.0.0.1 if on the same machine), and click Connect.

steps.title: 4 · Load a Template
steps.body: Browse the Template Library. Click 'Control' on any template to see its live parameter sliders. Click 'Launch TD' to open its .toe file automatically.

steps.title: 5 · Control Parameters Live
steps.body: Every slider in the parameter panel sends an OSC message to TouchDesigner in real time. Move a slider — see the result instantly in TD's viewport.

steps.title: 6 · Try AI Parameters
steps.body: Describe a mood in words — 'aggressive red electricity storm' — and Claude will translate it into all OSC parameter values automatically and apply them live.

tips: Check your firewall allows UDP on port 7000 (OSC send) and 7001 (OSC receive).
WebSocket (port 9980) enables richer two-way communication — required for SD Prompt and more.
For live VJ performance, leave parameter sliders open and use keyboard macros in TD for quick preset switching.
Use the AI Parameter Control to explore completely new visual territory in seconds — it's the fastest creative tool in the whole tab.
apiKeys: Anthropic — Claude for AI parameter generation
